missions.title: Where Am I?
missions.skill: Navigate Linux and confirm your location
missions.goal: Discover where you are, explore the available directories, and move to the correct destination.
missions.bigIdea: Linux always tracks your current working directory, and every relative movement begins from that location.
missions.briefing: You have entered the Hydra training account at /home/hydra. Before exploring the castle, you must learn how to identify your location, inspect the rooms around you, and enter the correct directory.

learn.explanation: pwd means print working directory. It answers: “Where am I right now?”
ls lists the files and directories in your current location.
cd means change directory. Add a directory name to move into that location.

walkthrough.title: Identify your location
walkthrough.text: Run pwd. Linux prints /home/hydra, which is the current working directory.

walkthrough.title: Look for the destination
walkthrough.text: Run ls. The output includes Documents, Downloads, and training.

walkthrough.title: Enter the directory
walkthrough.text: Run cd Documents. The command changes your location without printing a success message.

walkthrough.title: Confirm the move
walkthrough.text: Run pwd again. The new path is /home/hydra/Documents.

guidedPractice.instructions: Starting in /home/hydra, identify your location, list its contents, enter the Documents directory, and confirm your new location.
guidedPractice.successFeedback: Guided practice complete. You used pwd to identify the path, ls to find Documents, and cd to enter it.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: The terminal is safe to retry. One or more navigation steps are still missing.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use pwd, then ls, then cd Documents. Run pwd once more after changing directories.

commanderChallenge.instructions: You are back in /home/hydra. Discover the available destinations, move into Downloads, and prove that you arrived there.
steps: Confirm that Downloads is now your current location.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Think about the three actions you need to perform: inspect your surroundings, move to the destination, and confirm your final location.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Which commands list directory contents, change directories, and print the working directory?

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Try this sequence: ls, cd Downloads, pwd.

commanderChallenge.successFeedback: Commander Challenge complete. The terminal confirms that you reached /home/hydra/Downloads.
commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: The destination has not been confirmed yet.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: List the available directories if needed, use cd with the destination name, and use pwd to verify the final path.

missions.correctFeedback: Excellent navigation. You recognized the purpose of pwd, ls, and cd and used them in a meaningful sequence.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review which command identifies a location, which command lists contents, and which command changes directories.
missions.fenrirTip: pwd asks “Where am I?”, ls looks around the room, and cd walks through a doorway.
missions.debrief: You learned to identify the current working directory with pwd, inspect it with ls, and move into another directory with cd. On the exam, path or navigation language should trigger recognition of these commands.
missions.takeaway: Location → pwd. Contents → ls. Movement → cd.

missions.title: Build the Workspace
missions.skill: Build and verify a simple Linux workspace
missions.goal: Create an organized directory containing the required file and verify that the workspace is ready.
missions.bigIdea: Linux creates files and directories in your current location, so where you are matters as much as what command you run.
missions.briefing: The Hydra Commander needs a clean workspace for training records. You will create a directory, enter it, create an empty file, and verify that the file exists.

learn.explanation: mkdir means make directory. It creates a new directory with the name you provide.
cd enters the directory you created so the new file is placed inside the workspace.
touch can create an empty file when that file does not already exist.
After creating something, ls helps verify that its name appears in the directory.

walkthrough.title: Create the workspace
walkthrough.text: Run mkdir workshop. This adds a new workshop directory under /home/hydra.

walkthrough.title: Enter the workspace
walkthrough.text: Run cd workshop so new files are created inside that directory.

walkthrough.title: Create the file
walkthrough.text: Run touch notes.txt. This creates an empty training notes file.

walkthrough.title: Verify the result
walkthrough.text: Run ls. The output should include notes.txt.

guidedPractice.instructions: Create a directory named workshop, enter it, create notes.txt, and list the directory to verify the file.
steps: Create an empty file named notes.txt.
List the directory to verify the file.
guidedPractice.successFeedback: Guided practice complete. The workshop directory now contains notes.txt.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: The simulated workspace does not yet match the mission.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Create workshop with mkdir, enter it with cd, create notes.txt with touch, and finish with ls.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Prepare a reports workspace containing an empty status.txt file, then verify that the workspace is complete.
steps: Create an empty file named status.txt.
Verify that status.txt exists in the reports workspace.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Build the container first, enter it, create the file inside it, and then inspect the result.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Which commands make a directory, change your location, create an empty file, and list directory contents?

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Try this sequence: mkdir reports, cd reports, touch status.txt, ls.

commanderChallenge.successFeedback: Commander Challenge complete. /home/hydra/reports/status.txt exists and the result was verified with ls.
commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: The reports workspace is not complete yet.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Use the same four-part pattern: mkdir, cd, touch, then ls.

missions.correctFeedback: Workspace construction complete. You created and verified a directory-and-file structure using safe foundational commands.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review the order: create the directory, enter it, create the file, and verify the result.
missions.fenrirTip: mkdir builds the room, cd enters it, touch places a blank scroll inside, and ls checks your work.
missions.debrief: You learned to create directories with mkdir, create empty files with touch, and verify results with ls. Linux tasks often depend on running simple commands in the correct location and order.
missions.takeaway: Build → mkdir. Enter → cd. Create a file → touch. Verify → ls.

missions.title: Command Anatomy
missions.skill: Build commands from a command name, options, and arguments
missions.goal: Use echo to send exact messages to the terminal and use history to verify the commands you entered.
missions.bigIdea: A shell command is a structured request: the command chooses the tool, while options and arguments tell it what to do.
missions.briefing: The command console is online, but the Commander will only accept precisely formatted status messages. You will learn how the shell separates a command name from the information that follows it.

learn.explanation: echo is the command. Hydra is its argument, so the terminal displays Hydra.
Quotation marks keep words together as one argument when the text contains spaces.
history lists commands entered during the activity so you can review your work.

walkthrough.title: Send one word
walkthrough.text: Run echo Hydra. The terminal prints the argument Hydra.

walkthrough.title: Protect spaces
walkthrough.text: Run echo "mission ready". The quotes keep the two-word message together.

walkthrough.title: Review the session
walkthrough.text: Run history. The terminal lists the commands in the order you used them.

guidedPractice.instructions: Display Hydra, display the exact phrase mission ready with quotes, and review your command history.
steps: Run history to review both commands.
guidedPractice.successFeedback: Guided practice complete. You supplied arguments, protected a phrase with quotes, and reviewed the command history.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: The required messages or history review are still missing.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use echo for each message. Put quotation marks around mission ready, then run history.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Send the exact two-word status academy online, then prove the command is recorded in your history.
steps: Display academy online as one quoted phrase.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Choose a command that displays text, protect the phrase as one argument, and then inspect the session record.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: echo displays arguments, quotation marks protect spaces, and history shows previous commands.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run echo "academy online", then run history.

commanderChallenge.successFeedback: Commander Challenge complete. The exact status message was displayed and recorded.
commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: The exact quoted message and history review have not both been completed.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Display the required phrase with echo and quotes, then inspect history.

missions.correctFeedback: You correctly separated the command from its arguments and used quotes to preserve a phrase.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review how commands, options, arguments, and quotation marks shape a shell request.
missions.fenrirTip: Read a command from left to right: tool first, instructions second, target last.
missions.debrief: You used echo with simple and quoted arguments, then checked history. This command structure appears throughout Linux, even when the commands become more powerful.
missions.takeaway: Command chooses the tool. Options adjust behavior. Arguments provide the target or data.

missions.title: Expand the Shell
missions.skill: Recognize variables, quoting, and filename patterns
missions.goal: Use shell variables and wildcard patterns to produce predictable terminal results.
missions.bigIdea: Before a command runs, the shell can transform variables, quoted text, and wildcard patterns into usable values.
missions.briefing: A scout left instructions containing symbols instead of full paths and filenames. You must recognize how the shell expands those symbols before passing the result to a command.

learn.explanation: $HOME expands to the current user's home directory, /home/hydra.
The asterisk matches any filename ending in .txt in the current directory.
Double quotes preserve spaces so the phrase is handled together.

walkthrough.title: Expand a variable
walkthrough.text: Run echo $HOME. The shell substitutes the home-directory value.

walkthrough.title: Match a group
walkthrough.text: Run ls *.txt. The wildcard selects visible names ending in .txt.

walkthrough.title: Protect a phrase
walkthrough.text: Run echo "shell ready" so the space remains part of one phrase.

guidedPractice.instructions: Display your home directory variable, list the .txt files in your current directory with a wildcard, and display shell ready as a quoted phrase.
guidedPractice.successFeedback: Guided practice complete. Variables, wildcards, and quotes produced the expected values.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: One or more shell expansions are still missing.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use echo with $HOME, ls with *.txt, and echo with a quoted phrase.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Display the current username variable, find all .txt files with a wildcard, and send the quoted status expansion complete.
steps: Display expansion complete as one quoted phrase.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Use one variable, one filename wildcard, and one quoted phrase.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: $USER identifies the current user, *.txt matches text files, and quotes preserve a spaced message.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run echo $USER, ls *.txt, and echo "expansion complete".

commanderChallenge.successFeedback: Commander Challenge complete. All three shell expansion forms were used correctly.
commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: The variable, wildcard, and quoted-message requirements are not all complete.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Use echo with a user variable, ls with a text-file wildcard, and echo with a quoted status.

missions.correctFeedback: You recognized three transformations performed by the shell before a command completes.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review variables, wildcard matching, and quotation marks as separate shell behaviors.
missions.fenrirTip: When symbols appear in a command, ask what the shell will replace or preserve before the tool receives them.
missions.debrief: You expanded $HOME and $USER, selected filenames with *.txt, and preserved phrases with quotes. These behaviors make short commands flexible and precise.
missions.takeaway: $ expands a variable. * matches names. Quotes protect text.

missions.title: Ask Linux for Help
missions.skill: Choose an appropriate command-line help system
missions.goal: Open manual, option, and info documentation for unfamiliar commands.
missions.bigIdea: Linux does not expect you to memorize every option; skilled users know how to find authoritative help.
missions.objective: 2.2 Using the Command Line to Get Help
missions.briefing: A new set of tools has arrived without a printed guide. Instead of guessing, you will use the documentation already available from the command line.

learn.explanation: man opens the structured manual page for a command.
--help usually displays a concise usage summary and common options.
info opens topic-oriented documentation that may contain connected sections.

walkthrough.title: Open a manual
walkthrough.text: Run man ls to inspect the command's name and synopsis.

walkthrough.title: Request quick help
walkthrough.text: Run ls --help for a concise usage reference.

walkthrough.title: Open an info node
walkthrough.text: Run info mkdir for topic-oriented documentation.

guidedPractice.instructions: Open the ls manual, request ls option help, and open the mkdir info documentation.
guidedPractice.successFeedback: Guided practice complete. You used three standard command-line help paths.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: One or more documentation sources have not been opened.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use man with ls, --help with ls, and info with mkdir.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Research file-copy and file-move commands using a manual page, quick option help, and an info document.
steps: Open the manual for the copy command.
Request quick help from the copy command.
Open info documentation for the move command.
helpExamples: info COMMAND — open an info node

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Use the three documentation routes demonstrated in Guided Practice with the requested tools.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: The copy command is cp and the move command is mv.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run man cp, cp --help, and info mv.

commanderChallenge.successFeedback: Commander Challenge complete. You researched unfamiliar commands instead of guessing.
commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: All three requested documentation checks are not yet present.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Use a manual, a --help request, and an info node for the named tools.

missions.correctFeedback: You selected appropriate built-in documentation sources for different help needs.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review when to use man, --help, and info.
missions.fenrirTip: Experts do not avoid help; they reach the right help source quickly.
missions.debrief: You opened manual pages, requested concise option help, and used info documentation. These habits reduce errors and make unfamiliar commands safer.
missions.takeaway: Deep reference → man. Quick syntax → --help. Connected topics → info.

missions.title: Paths You Cannot See
missions.skill: Navigate absolute and relative paths and inspect hidden entries
missions.goal: Reveal hidden entries, inspect detailed listings, navigate by path, and verify the final location.
missions.bigIdea: Linux paths describe location precisely, while listing options reveal information that ordinary output may hide.
missions.briefing: A hidden Academy record and a distant training directory must be inspected. You will combine listing options with absolute and relative navigation.

learn.explanation: -a includes names beginning with a dot, plus . and ...
-l displays a long format with entry type and permission information.
An absolute path begins at / and identifies the same destination from any current directory.
.. means the parent directory relative to your current location.

walkthrough.title: Inspect details
walkthrough.text: Run ls -l to view entry types and permission-like details.

walkthrough.title: Use an absolute path
walkthrough.text: Run cd /home/hydra/training to move directly to training.

walkthrough.title: Move relatively
walkthrough.text: Run cd .., then pwd. You return to /home/hydra and verify it.

guidedPractice.instructions: Reveal hidden entries, request a long listing, move directly to training with an absolute path, return with .., and verify /home/hydra.
guidedPractice.successFeedback: Guided practice complete. You revealed hidden data and navigated with both path forms.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: The listing or path-navigation requirements are not all complete.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use both ls options, visit training by absolute path, return with .., and finish with pwd.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Inspect hidden and detailed entries, enter training using a relative path, return home using an absolute path, and prove your final location.
helpExamples: relative paths begin from the current directory

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Combine two listing options, two different path styles, and a final location check.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: -a reveals hidden names, -l shows detail, training is relative from home, and /home/hydra is absolute.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run ls -a, ls -l, cd training, cd /home/hydra, and pwd.

commanderChallenge.successFeedback: Commander Challenge complete. Hidden entries, details, and both path styles were handled correctly.
commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: The required listings, navigation forms, or final verification are incomplete.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Use -a and -l, navigate once relatively and once absolutely, then verify with pwd.

missions.correctFeedback: You combined listing options with absolute and relative navigation accurately.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review hidden entries, long listings, and how path starting points differ.
missions.fenrirTip: A leading slash starts at the filesystem root; no leading slash starts where your paws already stand.
missions.debrief: You revealed hidden entries, inspected a detailed listing, and navigated using absolute and relative paths. You also verified the resulting location instead of assuming success.
missions.takeaway: Hidden → -a. Details → -l. Rooted path → absolute. Current-location path → relative.

missions.title: Organize and Clean Up
missions.skill: Copy, move, rename, and safely remove files and empty directories
missions.goal: Transform a cluttered home directory into an exact required filesystem state.
missions.bigIdea: File-management commands are judged by the state they create, so verify destinations and remove only the intended targets.
missions.briefing: The training account contains reports, drafts, temporary files, and empty directories. You must preserve needed data, rename unfinished work, and safely remove clutter.

learn.explanation: cp creates a second file while leaving the source in place.
mv changes a file's path; in the same directory, that renames it.
rm removes the named file. Verify the target before running it.
rmdir removes a directory only when it contains nothing.

walkthrough.title: Create a destination
walkthrough.text: Run mkdir archive before copying a file into it.

walkthrough.title: Copy required data
walkthrough.text: Run cp report.txt archive/report.txt. Both copies now exist.

walkthrough.title: Remove clutter
walkthrough.text: Run rm temp.txt and rmdir empty, then list the result.

guidedPractice.instructions: Create archive, copy report.txt into it, rename draft.txt to final.txt, remove temp.txt, remove the empty directory, and list the result.
guidedPractice.successFeedback: Guided practice complete. Required files were preserved and clutter was removed.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: The filesystem does not yet match the required organized state.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Create the destination, copy the report, rename the draft, remove the file and empty directory, then list.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Create completed, copy mission.txt into it, rename notes.txt to briefing.txt, remove scratch.txt and unused, then verify the final state.
helpExamples: cp — preserve a source while copying

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Create the container, preserve one file, rename another, remove two kinds of clutter, and verify the state.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Use mkdir, cp, mv, rm, rmdir, and ls with the names given in the mission.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run mkdir completed, cp mission.txt completed/mission.txt, mv notes.txt briefing.txt, rm scratch.txt, rmdir unused, and ls.

commanderChallenge.successFeedback: Commander Challenge complete. The home directory now matches the required organized state.
commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: The required copied, renamed, or removed entries are not all correct.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Check that the source copy remains, the renamed source is gone, and both clutter targets were removed.

missions.correctFeedback: You organized the filesystem by its final state while preserving every required source.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review the different effects of copy, move, file removal, and empty-directory removal.
missions.fenrirTip: Before removing anything, name the target, predict what will remain, and verify afterward.
missions.debrief: You copied files without losing their sources, renamed files with mv, removed files with rm, and removed empty directories with rmdir. State-based grading accepted the result rather than requiring one rigid order.
missions.takeaway: Preserve → cp. Relocate or rename → mv. Remove file → rm. Remove empty directory → rmdir.

missions.title: Pack the Archive
missions.skill: Create, inspect, and extract compressed archives
missions.goal: Protect the training directory in a compressed archive and verify its contents.
missions.bigIdea: An archive groups files into one transportable unit, while compression reduces the space that unit requires.
missions.objective: 3.1 Archiving Files on the Command Line
missions.briefing: Training records must cross the mountain intact. Create a compressed archive, inspect it before trusting it, and practice extraction.

learn.explanation: tar collects training; z applies gzip compression; f names the archive.
t lists archive contents without extracting them.
x extracts the compressed archive.

walkthrough.title: Inspect before extraction
walkthrough.text: Run tar -tzf training.tar.gz and confirm training appears.

guidedPractice.instructions: Create training.tar.gz from training, inspect it, and extract it.
guidedPractice.successFeedback: Archive creation, inspection, and extraction complete.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: The archive workflow is incomplete.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use tar with c, then t, then x; keep z and f in each command.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Create records.tar.gz from Documents, inspect it, and extract it.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Create, inspect, then extract.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Use the same c/t/x pattern with records.tar.gz and Documents.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run tar -czf records.tar.gz Documents, tar -tzf records.tar.gz, and tar -xzf records.tar.gz.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: The records archive workflow is incomplete.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Create the named archive from Documents before listing and extracting it.

missions.correctFeedback: You treated inspection as part of the archive workflow.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review create, list, and extract modes.
missions.fenrirTip: Never trust a sealed pack until you inspect what it contains.
missions.debrief: You created gzip-compressed tar archives, listed their contents, and extracted them.
missions.takeaway: Create → c. Inspect → t. Extract → x. gzip → z. Archive name → f.

missions.title: Find the Signal
missions.skill: Search, sample, count, and extract useful text
missions.goal: Turn logs and delimited data into concise evidence.
missions.bigIdea: Text tools answer different questions: which lines match, which lines matter first or last, how many exist, and which fields are needed.
missions.objective: 3.2 Searching and Extracting Data from Files
missions.briefing: The patrol log is noisy and the score roster contains more data than the Commander needs. Extract only the evidence that answers each question.

learn.explanation: grep prints lines containing ERROR.
head samples the start of a file; tail samples its end.
wc -l counts lines.
cut uses comma as the delimiter and returns field one.

walkthrough.title: Count and extract
walkthrough.text: Count log lines and extract score names.

guidedPractice.instructions: Find ERROR, inspect the first and last log entries, count lines, and extract score names.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: One or more text checks are missing.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use grep, head, tail, wc -l, and cut.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Find WARN, inspect the log edges, count it, and extract the score names.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Use one tool per question.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Search WARN, sample both ends, count lines, then select CSV field one.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run grep WARN events.log, head events.log, tail events.log, wc -l events.log, and cut -d, -f1 scores.csv.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: The requested evidence set is incomplete.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Match each question to grep, head/tail, wc, or cut.

missions.correctFeedback: You selected tools by the question each tool answers.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review search, sampling, counting, and field extraction.
missions.fenrirTip: Do not read the whole forest when one track answers the question.
missions.debrief: You searched logs, sampled file edges, counted lines, and extracted CSV fields.
missions.takeaway: Match → grep. Edges → head/tail. Count → wc. Field → cut.

missions.title: Build the Pipeline
missions.skill: Connect commands with pipes and save output with redirection
missions.goal: Filter command output and route the result to the screen or a file.
missions.bigIdea: A pipeline lets one command's output become the next command's input, while redirection chooses where the final result goes.
missions.objective: 3.2 Searching and Extracting Data from Files
missions.briefing: The Commander wants compact reports without temporary manual work. Connect tools so data flows directly from source to filter to destination.

learn.explanation: | sends matching lines from grep into wc.
> saves output to a file, replacing prior contents.
The second command receives only the first command's output.

walkthrough.title: Connect two tools
walkthrough.text: Count matching INFO lines through a pipe.

walkthrough.title: Verify the artifact
walkthrough.text: List errors.txt to confirm it exists.

guidedPractice.instructions: Count INFO lines through a pipe, save ERROR lines to errors.txt, and verify the file.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: The pipeline or saved result is missing.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use | to connect commands and > to create errors.txt.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Send WARN lines through head, save them to warnings.txt, and verify the file.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Search, sample, save, verify.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Connect grep WARN to head, then redirect.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run grep WARN events.log | head > warnings.txt, then ls warnings.txt.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: warnings.txt has not been produced and verified.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Pipe grep into head before redirecting to warnings.txt.

missions.correctFeedback: You treated output as a stream that can be transformed and routed.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review pipes versus redirection.
missions.fenrirTip: A pipe passes the trail onward; redirection chooses where the trail ends.
missions.debrief: You connected commands and saved final output to files.
missions.takeaway: Connect → |. Save/replace → >. Verify → ls.

missions.title: Your First Script
missions.skill: Create and run a simple shell script with an argument
missions.goal: Build an executable script that prints a supplied mission name.
missions.bigIdea: A script turns tested command steps into a reusable tool whose arguments supply changing input.
missions.briefing: The same status message must be produced for different missions. Store the command in a script and let its first argument provide the changing name.

learn.explanation: The shebang identifies the shell used to interpret the script.
$1 represents the first argument supplied when the script runs.
chmod +x permits the script to run directly.
./ selects the script in the current directory and north becomes $1.

walkthrough.title: Add the command
walkthrough.text: Append an echo command that uses $1.

walkthrough.title: Permit and run
walkthrough.text: Make it executable, then pass north.

guidedPractice.instructions: Create patrol.sh with a shebang and echo $1, make it executable, and run it with north.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: The script workflow is incomplete.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Create, append, permit, and execute in that order.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Create report.sh with a shebang and echo $1, make it executable, and run it with academy.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Repeat the four-part script pattern with new names.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Use report.sh and pass academy as argument one.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run echo '#!/bin/sh' > report.sh, echo 'echo $1' >> report.sh, chmod +x report.sh, and ./report.sh academy.

commanderChallenge.successFeedback: Commander script executed with its argument.
commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: report.sh is not fully created and executed.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Build both lines, permit execution, then pass academy.

missions.correctFeedback: You converted a command into a reusable argument-driven script.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review shebang, script body, permission, and execution.
missions.fenrirTip: Automate only what you can explain step by step.
missions.debrief: You created scripts, used $1, enabled execution, and supplied arguments.
missions.takeaway: Interpreter → shebang. Input → $1. Permission → chmod +x. Run → ./script.

missions.title: Automate the Patrol
missions.skill: Use a loop in a repeatable shell script
missions.goal: Create and run a script that repeats one action for multiple patrol names.
missions.bigIdea: A loop expresses repetition once, reducing duplicated commands and inconsistent results.
missions.briefing: Two patrol names must be processed the same way. Replace duplicated commands with a single loop that applies one action to each item.

learn.command: for item in alpha beta; do echo $item; done
learn.explanation: for assigns each word to item; do/done contain the repeated action.
The body uses the current loop value.
Running the script produces the repeated outputs.

walkthrough.title: Add the loop
walkthrough.command: echo 'for item in alpha beta; do echo $item; done' >> loop.sh

guidedPractice.instructions: Create loop.sh, append the alpha/beta loop, make it executable, and run it.
helpExamples: echo 'for item in alpha beta; do echo $item; done' >> loop.sh
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: The loop script workflow is incomplete.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Create the file, append the loop, permit it, then run it.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Create sweep.sh with a north/south loop, make it executable, and run it.
helpExamples: for NAME in VALUES; do ACTION; done

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Reuse the loop pattern with two different values.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: The values are north and south; the variable is zone.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run echo '#!/bin/sh' > sweep.sh, echo 'for zone in north south; do echo $zone; done' >> sweep.sh, chmod +x sweep.sh, and ./sweep.sh.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: sweep.sh is not fully created and run.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Build the loop script, permit it, and execute it.

missions.correctFeedback: You replaced repeated commands with a single controlled loop.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review the for/in/do/done structure.
missions.fenrirTip: When only the target changes, a loop should carry the repeated work.
missions.debrief: You stored loop logic in executable scripts and applied one command consistently to multiple values.
missions.takeaway: Values → in. Repeated action → do/done. Current value → $variable.

missions.title: Distribution Detective
missions.skill: Identify Linux from standard system evidence
missions.goal: Inspect distribution identity, kernel family, and architecture.
missions.bigIdea: Evidence inside a system identifies it more reliably than appearance or branding.
missions.objective: 1.1 Linux Evolution and Popular Operating Systems
missions.briefing: An unlabeled cloud image must be identified before use.

learn.explanation: The standard file identifies the distribution.
uname reports the kernel family.
-m reports machine architecture.

guidedPractice.instructions: Collect all three identity signals.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: Evidence is incomplete.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use os-release and both uname forms.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Independently reconstruct the image identity.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Use one file and two system queries.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Inspect os-release, kernel, and machine architecture.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run cat /etc/os-release, uname, and uname -m.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: All three signals are required.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Gather distribution, kernel, and architecture.

missions.correctFeedback: You identified Linux from standard evidence.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review the three identity signals.
missions.fenrirTip: Labels can lie; system evidence does not.
missions.debrief: You identified a distribution, kernel, and architecture as you would on cloud, desktop, or embedded Linux.
missions.takeaway: Distribution → os-release. Kernel → uname. Architecture → uname -m.

missions.title: Open Source Toolbox
missions.skill: Recognize open-source tools by workload
missions.goal: Verify tools for desktop, development, server, and package work.
missions.bigIdea: Open-source applications form an ecosystem in which each tool serves a recognizable workload.
missions.briefing: Verify that a workstation supports four required workloads.

learn.explanation: Firefox is an open-source browser.
Python supports software development.
NGINX serves web content.
apt-get works with package repositories.

guidedPractice.instructions: Locate all four tools.
steps: Check browser, language, server, and package tool.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: A workload is missing.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use which with every tool.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Prove all four workload roles are available.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Check one tool per workload.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Use Firefox, Python, NGINX, and apt-get.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run which firefox, which python3, which nginx, and which apt-get.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: All roles must be checked.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Locate each named tool.

missions.correctFeedback: You mapped tools to workloads.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review application roles.
missions.fenrirTip: Choose tools by the work they perform.
missions.debrief: You verified representative desktop, development, server, and package applications.
missions.takeaway: Desktop → Firefox. Development → Python. Server → NGINX. Packages → apt-get.

missions.title: The License Gate
missions.skill: Distinguish copyleft and permissive obligations
missions.goal: Inspect license notices and locate redistribution conditions.
missions.bigIdea: A license grants permissions with conditions that govern redistribution.
missions.briefing: Review two packages before approving redistribution.

learn.explanation: GPL carries reciprocal source obligations.
BSD permits broad reuse with retained notices.
grep isolates a specific condition.

guidedPractice.instructions: Read both notices and find the GPL source rule.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: Evidence is incomplete.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Read both and search GPL.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Read both notices and find BSD attribution.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Compare both, then locate the requested condition.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Search LICENSE-BSD for attribution.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run cat LICENSE-GPL, cat LICENSE-BSD, and grep attribution LICENSE-BSD.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: Evidence is incomplete.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Read both and search BSD.

missions.correctFeedback: You based judgment on license evidence.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review copyleft and permissive conditions.
missions.fenrirTip: Open source means permission with terms.
missions.debrief: You compared license grants and practical redistribution obligations.
missions.takeaway: GPL → reciprocal source terms. BSD → permissive reuse with notices.

missions.title: Linux at Work
missions.skill: Verify a secure Linux work session before handling project data
missions.goal: Confirm terminal, identity, shell, and workplace safeguards.
missions.bigIdea: Before handling work data, verify who you are, where the session runs, and which security expectations govern the task.
missions.objective: 1.4 ICT Skills and Working in Linux
missions.briefing: Before opening private project data on a local, virtual, or cloud Linux host, verify the session and safeguards.

learn.explanation: tty identifies the active terminal device.
whoami confirms the active account.
$SHELL identifies the interpreter.
The checklist connects trusted sessions, unique passwords, and private-data care.

guidedPractice.instructions: Verify endpoint, identity, shell, and safeguards.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: Verification is incomplete.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Check all four signals.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Verify the work session and locate the unique-password safeguard before accepting private data.
steps: Verify endpoint, user, shell, checklist, and password rule.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Verify the technical session, then the human safeguard.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Check tty, identity, shell, checklist, and unique password.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run tty, whoami, echo $SHELL, cat privacy-checklist.txt, and grep "unique password" privacy-checklist.txt.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: Technical and password evidence are required.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Verify session and locate the password rule.

missions.correctFeedback: You treated workplace security as one verified pre-work decision.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review session and safeguard evidence.
missions.fenrirTip: Verify the den, the identity at the door, and the rules inside.
missions.debrief: You verified a cohesive Linux work session before handling data; the habit applies to terminals on local systems, VMs, and cloud hosts.
missions.takeaway: Endpoint → tty. Identity → whoami. Shell → $SHELL. Safeguards → checklist.

missions.title: Choose the Right System
missions.skill: Match an operating-system release style to workload requirements
missions.goal: Use written requirements and system identity evidence to choose a stable server platform.
missions.bigIdea: The best operating system is the one whose interface, support cycle, and release model fit the workload.
missions.briefing: Choose a platform for an Academy server by comparing requirements with system evidence.

learn.explanation: Requirements define stability, support, and administration needs.
Desktop priorities may favor a GUI and faster feature changes.
os-release identifies the candidate platform.

guidedPractice.instructions: Read both requirement sets and identify the candidate system.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: Comparison is incomplete.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Read all three files.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Verify the candidate fits a stable command-line server workload.
steps: Review server needs, candidate identity, and kernel.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Compare workload needs to platform evidence.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Read server requirements and os-release, then confirm Linux.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run cat server-requirements.txt, cat /etc/os-release, and uname.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: The choice lacks complete evidence.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Review requirements and system identity.

missions.correctFeedback: You chose by workload fit rather than preference.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review interface and lifecycle needs.
missions.fenrirTip: A good platform serves the mission longer than the novelty of its features.
missions.debrief: You compared workload requirements, release priorities, and Linux identity evidence.
missions.takeaway: Workload needs → requirements. Platform lifecycle → release model. Candidate → os-release.

missions.title: Inspect the Machine
missions.skill: Inspect CPU, memory, and storage-device evidence
missions.goal: Verify that required hardware resources are visible to Linux.
missions.bigIdea: Linux exposes hardware through system files, device entries, and resource-reporting commands.
missions.briefing: Confirm the virtual training host can see its processor, memory, and primary disk.

learn.explanation: cpuinfo exposes processor information.
free summarizes memory capacity and availability.
Block devices appear beneath /dev.

guidedPractice.instructions: Verify CPU, memory, and disk.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: A hardware check is missing.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Inspect all three resources.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Prove processor, available memory, and storage visibility.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Use one source per hardware class.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: CPU is in /proc, memory uses free, disk is /dev/sda.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run cat /proc/cpuinfo, free, and ls /dev/sda.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: All hardware evidence is required.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Check CPU, memory, and disk.

missions.correctFeedback: You verified hardware through Linux interfaces.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review /proc, memory tools, and /dev.
missions.fenrirTip: Ask the operating system what it can see before blaming the hardware.
missions.debrief: You inspected processor, memory, and storage-device evidence.
missions.takeaway: CPU → /proc/cpuinfo. Memory → free. Devices → /dev.

missions.title: Follow the Data
missions.skill: Inspect processes, memory, kernel messages, and logs
missions.goal: Build a concise system-health picture from the correct data sources.
missions.bigIdea: Linux separates live process state, resource state, kernel messages, and persistent logs into distinct evidence sources.
missions.briefing: A host reports trouble. Inspect live state and stored messages before deciding what happened.

learn.explanation: ps lists a process snapshot.
top summarizes active processes and resources.
dmesg displays kernel messages.
System logs commonly live under /var/log.

walkthrough.title: Inspect messages
walkthrough.text: Run dmesg and read the log.

guidedPractice.instructions: Inspect ps, top, free, dmesg, and the Hydra log.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: Evidence is incomplete.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Use all five checks.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Collect live process, memory, kernel, and persistent-log evidence.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Use a different source for each evidence class.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Run ps, top, free, dmesg, and read the Hydra log.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run ps, top, free, dmesg, and cat /var/log/hydra.log.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: Every evidence class is required.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Check live and stored sources.

missions.correctFeedback: You separated live state from stored messages.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review where each data type lives.
missions.fenrirTip: The freshest track and the oldest record answer different questions.
missions.debrief: You inspected process tables, memory, kernel messages, and logs.
missions.takeaway: Processes → ps/top. Memory → free. Kernel → dmesg. Logs → /var/log.

missions.title: Check the Network
missions.skill: Verify address, route, name resolution, and reachability
missions.goal: Test the four basic requirements of a functioning network connection.
missions.bigIdea: Network diagnosis becomes manageable when address, route, DNS, and reachability are checked separately.
missions.briefing: The Academy host may be connected but unable to reach a named service. Test each network layer in order.

learn.explanation: ip addr shows interface addresses.
ip route shows the default gateway path.
host resolves a name to an address.
ping tests whether a destination responds.

guidedPractice.instructions: Verify address, route, DNS, and reachability.
guidedPractice.incorrectFeedback: A network layer is unchecked.
guidedPractice.retryHint: Test all four layers.

commanderChallenge.instructions: Verify the host can identify itself, find a route, resolve server.local, and reach the gateway.

hints.label: Concept Hint
hints.text: Check local configuration before external reachability.

hints.label: Recognition Hint
hints.text: Use ip addr, ip route, host, and ping.

hints.label: Command Reveal
hints.text: Run ip addr, ip route, host server.local, and ping 192.0.2.1.

commanderChallenge.incorrectFeedback: All four network checks are required.
commanderChallenge.retryHint: Check address, route, name, and ping.

missions.correctFeedback: You diagnosed the network by layer.
missions.incorrectFeedback: Review address, route, DNS, and reachability.
missions.fenrirTip: Start at your paws, then follow the path outward.
missions.debrief: You separated local addressing, routing, name resolution, and reachability.
missions.takeaway: Address → ip addr. Route → ip route. DNS → host. Reachability → ping.
